A mechanical dragon descends diagonally from above, wings folded, claws slightly open, landing on the edge of the museum steps with minimal vibration and stable impact absorption. shot2: Shot 2 hard cuts from previous shot, medium close-up at eye level with slight upward angle. Uses the depth of the museum hall as leading lines. Foreground features wet traces and reflective stone brought indoors by rain. Mid-ground focuses on the dragon lowering its head and delicately picking up a metallic spool with its teeth. The silver-blue thread glints under cold white ceiling lights and side neon, creating narrow highlights. Background exhibition space blurs into orderly geometric light planes. Camera slowly pushes in, revealing detailed mechanical jaw articulation and subtle spool rotation.
shot3: Shot 3 uses an action-matched cut from previous shot, extreme close-up at eye level focusing on the needle’s eye held by the front claw. Composition slants the needle across frame for strong directionality. Shallow depth of field keeps only the needle’s edge, tiny claw joint, and thread tip sharply in focus. Background museum lighting and rain-soaked neon blur into soft color blocks. Cold side lighting outlines metal edges. Camera uses an ultra-slow push to create a sense of lock-on.
shot4: Shot 4 hard cuts via whip pan into the connecting corridor, full shot at eye level with lateral follow. The corridor links the museum to the subway station. Glass walls show blurred city lights outside. Interior floor is wet and mirror-like. The dragon carries the spool, front claw firmly holding the giant needle. Gait shifts from cautious to steady buildup. Tail and wingtips swing rhythmically with increasing speed. The silver-blue thread trails behind in a long arc, fluttering slightly with airflow. Camera tracks forward along its path, occasionally nudging forward to emphasize motion.
shot5: Shot 5 hard cuts to subway platform, medium close-up at low angle from the side. Platform columns and light strips form strong perspective lines. Focus is on the needle’s eye and front claw. Side light cuts diagonally from the dark side where the train hasn’t arrived, illuminating water droplets trapped in scale crevices as cold bright particles. After steady buildup, the dragon makes its first thread-feed attempt. Claw extends precisely, thread sliding like a thin silver beam toward the needle’s eye—yet veers slightly at the last moment due to air disturbance. Camera briefly pushes in and freezes. The feeding motion syncs with a sharp high-frequency metallic tremor.
shot6: Shot 6 hard cuts with compressed space into the transfer passage, extreme close-up from above. Ceiling creates a long, oppressive tunnel effect. Foreground shows fast-moving thread reflections. Mid-ground locks only the needle’s edge and thread tip. Background artificial lights stretch into cold white stripes. While moving, the dragon subtly adjusts wrist angle. Thread nearly grazes the needle’s edge, sparking a tiny cold flash. Missed by a hair. Camera does a micro-rush then instantly jerks to a halt. Rain echoes in the passage, sounding emptier, heightening the tension of near-miss.
shot7: Shot 7 match-cuts via motion direction to elevated walkway at the amusement park, wide overhead with slight tilt. Walkway curves and distant rotating ride lights form dynamic background. Colors remain muted, only sparse blue-purple neon diffusing in rain mist. Dragon pauses at the edge, facing wind, raising claw to let the silver-blue thread sway freely before stabilizing. It finely rotates wrist and tightens shoulder structure based on wind direction, completing a higher-precision calibration. Camera orbits slightly, showing both wind flow and thread transitioning from trembling to straight. Mood shifts from tense to highly focused.
